title: LLM assistants in CS1 and instructor visibility

entries.query_str: what do instructors actually want to see about how students use ai assistants. any interview/survey studies 2024-2025
entries.answer:
Several interview and survey studies with CS instructors converge on a few needs [1][2][3]:

- **Who is stuck, not just who is using the assistant.** Usage counts alone weren't seen as useful; instructors want to know which students are struggling unproductively [1].
- **Context for intervention.** Instructors want to see *what the student was trying to do* (the code and the prompt together) before stepping in, rather than an alert with no context [2].
- **Over-reliance signals.** Concern about students pasting assignment text and taking full solutions; interest in seeing prompt patterns like "give me the code" [1][3].
- **Low time cost.** TAs in large courses said any tool must take seconds per student, not minutes [2].
- **Privacy and trust.** Some instructors were uneasy about surveillance and preferred aggregate views or opt-in individual views [3].

entries.answer: One survey reported most TAs would spend **under a minute per flagged student** during a live lab before moving on, and preferred tools that let them triage in seconds and dig in only when needed [1]. Treat that as one study's finding rather than a general rule.
